text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N2","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT :- 1) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 24-32 HRC. 2) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"Note N2 specifies a hardness of 24-32 HRC but does not state at which manufacturing stage the heat treatment is to be applied (e.g., before or after final machining). Without this, the machinist cannot plan the process sequence, risking dimensional errors or inability to machine hardened material. The designer should add the stage at which the toughening applies.","recommended_correction":"Update note N2 to specify when the heat treatment is to be performed relative to machining and surface treatment."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"NOTE : # MATERIAL : EN-91 # FINISH : E.N.P. # MACHINING :"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D1","page":1,"quote":"-0.007"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D2","page":1,"quote":"-0.020"}],"comment":"Note N3 calls for an E.N.P. (electroless nickel plating) finish, while dimensions D1 and D2 show tight negative tolerances (-0.007 mm and -0.020 mm) typical of shaft fits. Plating adds thickness that will shift these features out of tolerance if not accounted for, potentially causing assembly interference. The designer should either specify that the tolerances are after plating or reduce the pre-plate dimensions by the plating thickness.","recommended_correction":"Add a note stating that dimensions D1 and D2 apply after plating, or adjust the nominal sizes to allow for the specified E.N.P. thickness."}]}
